llm_summary: The run assembled several useful defensive tools, including Disarm+, Power Through, and upgraded Bash, but entered the final Sentry fight at only 26 HP. The clearest tactical failure occurred during that fight: at 12 HP, the agent spent actions on Rage and Pummel while an enemy was attacking, then ended the turn without playing the legal Power Through. Earlier, choosing to smith at 59/80 HP after the Lagavulin fight also prioritized an upgrade over recovery and likely left less margin for the remaining Act 1 combats.

llm_lessons.title: At critical HP, prioritize immediate survival over setup
llm_lessons.situation: When HP is low and an enemy is attacking, especially in a multi-enemy fight, compare every damage or setup play against the strongest available block option.
llm_lessons.lesson: Do not spend a low-HP turn on Rage or other non-defensive setup while an attack is incoming. In this state, play the legal Power Through or otherwise maximize immediate mitigation before pursuing damage.
evidence_points: On turn 3 of the Sentry fight, the player had 12/80 HP, the middle Sentry had Intent ATTACK, and Power Through was a legal alternative.
The chosen sequence was Play Rage, Play Pummel, Play Defend, Play Defend, then End turn; Power Through was still legal immediately before ending the turn.
The run died in the following Sentry combat, with the final logged state still showing three Sentries alive.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The logged state explicitly presents an attacking enemy and a playable defensive card at critical HP. Although exact incoming damage is unavailable, choosing setup and then ending without Power Through gave up a clear survival opportunity.

llm_lessons.title: After a damaging elite fight, healing can be worth more than a second upgrade
llm_lessons.situation: At a campfire after an elite or other costly combat, when below full HP and several Act 1 fights remain, favor recovery unless the upgrade is essential to survive a known upcoming fight.
llm_lessons.lesson: Reassess smithing at moderate or low HP instead of upgrading automatically. Preserving a larger HP buffer can be more valuable than improving a card when the route still contains multiple combats.
evidence_points: After the Lagavulin combat ended at 53/80 HP, the next campfire at floor 8 showed both rest and smith as legal alternatives.
The agent chose smith and upgraded Disarm while remaining at 59/80 HP, rather than restoring HP.
The next logged combats reduced HP to 23/80 after the Acid Slime/Slaver fight, then to 20/80 after the Looter fight, before the fatal Sentry combat.
llm_lessons.reasoning: The run had already paid a substantial HP cost for the elite and then continued through several combats without a healing choice. The later HP collapse shows that maintaining a buffer was important, though the exact counterfactual benefit of resting cannot be proven.
